meaning_by_symbol.PS: ring the bell briefly at each Bottom corner at moderate intensity; warm the joined edges for 12 seconds
meaning_by_symbol.CD: use dim light on the Bottom face and bright light on the opposite face for 12 seconds, holding still
meaning_by_symbol.LF: dim or faint overall, and quiet
meaning_by_symbol.HB: a hot bright corner and ticking
meaning_by_symbol.OA: alternating pulses on opposite faces, a two-tone hum, and edge flash
meaning_by_symbol.TB: hot all over, dim red, rumble, and gritty
meaning_by_symbol.CV: hollow tap, dark center, and thin hum
meaning_by_symbol.ES: too bright, layered hum, and some faces frozen or unresponsive
meaning_by_symbol.HS: competing tones, two configurations, and edge shimmer
meaning_by_symbol.RC: one face bright and vibrating, with a high whine, while the others are normal
meaning_by_symbol.HI: all faces blazing white, harsh buzz, and hot
meaning_by_symbol.BS: edges wobble, edges bulge, and muffled hum
meaning_by_symbol.DE: light drifts, edges are blurred, and hum wavers
meaning_by_symbol.LK: dim corners, fading edges, and leak state

reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry compositional paradigm is supported. Although several symbols share letters with other entries (e.g. B/T/L/R/F/Bk as face labels, and larger codes like LF, FR, HB, PS, CD), there is no minimal-pair frame where recurring parts alternate with stable, predictable contributions to whole meanings. In particular, the standalone face symbols do not appear as recoverable morphemes inside any longer code, and apparent overlaps such as LI/PI/HI or LF/FR/TB/HB are not compositionally interpretable from the supplied meanings. Under the evidence requirement and opaque-index test, the safest analysis is a flat lexicon with no segmented entries.
